replies.body:
Ugh, "It'd cost more". I hate it when money intervenes with perfect solutions. Honestly, if more players are playing on 1.8 during the 1.7/1.8 time, those were mostly just people that don't come back to Avicus after playing or are just not competitive. 1.7 for competitive community with less campers, bow spammers and targeters (pisses me off because these are allowed and it's not fun to play with these kind of people) and more challenging games. Also better hit detection and kb, and less lag.

This will encourage players to go to the competitive community, thus encouraging participation in tournaments and more teams. Also I think it makes more sense as well. 

Only downside ides is money :/. If we could have the same server supporting 1.8 on one game menu and 1.7 on another that'd be pretty cool. It's kind of like ranked and unranked on BadLion or Kohi.

replies.author: keenanjt
replies.body:
No, because the goal of Atlas is to improve the server. If this means bringing in more players, that's awesome, but it's not going to magically do that.

Why?

Tiny audience: I don't see us every reverting back to 1.7. It was nearly 3 years ago and today, only an estimated 8% of the Minecraft servers out there are hosting that version specifically. I wouldn't be surprised if an even smaller portion of players are on 1.7 as well. The competitive world might be different (more 1.7 users), but that still doesn't persuade me. That audience is not the audience that is going to be the easiest to attract.

Support for 1.7, urgh: Note that writing a 1.7 plugin is hardly any different than writing a 1.8 plugin. But maintaining the two and hosting separate servers and going through this work to attract the likes of such a small portion of the Minecraft community... That's not an easy task, nor an endeavor worth taking in my opinion. Every update we make would have to be further tested on both versions rigorously, libraries that we use have ended support and updates for old versions which means they have bugs and we must integrate those old versions with the hopes they work properly, different versions of our plugins must be maintained, etc. There are many issues of which you may not be aware.

replies.author: Sevoo
replies.body:
I'm going to be completely honest here. If the community liked MCZone the best, then why are you guys going further away from the MCZone like feel? It's kind of like the Minecraft updates.

Mojang's mindset is "the more the merrier" but they fail to see that maybe less is better. An example is the update from 1.5 to 1.6. Mostly all we had was horses. as this update successful? Very!

The update to 1.6 to 1.7. This was the first update that had A LOT of features (ex. like a gagillion new biomes). This update, and I believe all of you agree, was one of the best updates ever. It had better kb, better hit detection and the sprint button that replaced the old double tap "w" mechanic and added a lot of features but with no negative impacts on PvP. Then 1.8 came along, with the same kind mindset of more better, but there was a difference. Hit detection and kb became really bad compared to 1.7, and also Mojang's attempt to make the game smoother was only a success for a minority of people. 1.8 was a lot more GPU based than it was CPU based, so only the PCs with strong video cards saw a positive difference in FPS. Most other people with old PCs which already had bad FPS had even worse FPS with 1.8 (ex. when I had my old 7 year old PC, now 8 and a half years old, I used to get 40 FPS on 1.7 and 10 FPS on 1.8, even with minimal settings and OptiFine. Then 1.9 came along and same story. Worse FPS worse PvP mechanics (I mean seriously what do you expect from an update called "The Combat Update" from a game mostly directed to 7 year olds) and overall worse gameplay. 

What you guys are doing isn't much different. You're trying to make the server better, and in the long run more features should result into more players, but at this point it just doesn't. 

This is only my opinion, though I'm pretty sure a lot of us agree.
